svg.title: The stage graph of run_pipeline.py
svg.desc: Three bands. The top band, drawn with dashed borders and a marked spine, is what an agent owes before the runner can start: pass V over the rendered pages, passes A0 to A4, pass A5, and three hand-curated input files. The middle band is the fourteen deterministic stages the runner executes in order, from prompts through to manifest, wrapping left to right across three rows. Three stages are gates that exit non-zero and stop the run: structures, translations and verify. A dotted line links stage 7 to stage 12, which run the same script twice, once to publish the gold the resolvers read and once to pick up what they produced. The bottom of the middle band is the deliverable tree every stage writes into.
svg.text: One patent in, a complete deliverable out
python3 run_pipeline.py --patent-id <ID> · fourteen deterministic stages · three of them refuse to pass until a human supplies something
NOT RUN BY THIS SCRIPT · an agent owes these before the runner will start
pass V · agent, one per page
reads the rendered page images, not the OCR
assumes the annotation is wrong until proven
the curated tables start empty; the gates fill the list
Stage 1 renders those prompts into output/prompts/<ID>/ for the patent being run. If any pass is missing the runner names it, its rendered prompt and its output path, then stops.
RUN BY THIS SCRIPT · in this order, skipping any stage whose inputs and outputs still hash to what it last ran with
fill the patent id into the
every key seeded with the ID
stops if Chinese that can reach
counts read off the run, route
every SVG also as a JPG, for
readers that will not render SVG
the same script as stage 7, run
the review queue the UI reads;
sha256 of every artifact and of
gold/ provenance/ verification/ structures/ svg/ manifest.json

Every file here is listed in manifest.json with the stage that made it and the hashes it came from. Anything present that no stage produced is listed with a null stage, not quietly counted as current.
LEGEND · every distinction below is carried by a shape or a word as well as by a colour, so the diagram survives greyscale
solid thin border · deterministic stage, run by run_pipeline.py
thick border, octagon marked GATE · exits non-zero and stops the run
dashed border, marked spine · NOT run by the script; an agent or a human produces it
medium border, no number · the deliverable tree, not a stage
solid arrow · the next stage consumes what this one wrote
dotted arrow · the same script, run a second time over more inputs
--from <stage> starts at a stage and runs everything after. --only <stage> runs one.
--plan prints this graph as text and stops. --force ignores every up-to-date check.
A stage that failed last time always runs again: the manifest remembers, mtimes do not.
